title: Opposing thermal changes left little net warming at 210 British butterfly sites with fixed European atlas scores
abstract: We tested whether weak butterfly thermal change persists with fixed historical European atlas scores and whether opposite changes cancel. We used UKBMS records through 2024, CLIMBER scores and GHCN_CAMS air temperature. At 210 long-running British sites, warming and cooling areas between early and late thermal distribution functions were 0.0429 and 0.0336 C. Their difference was 0.0093 C (spatial-block 95% interval -0.0074 to 0.0256), only 12% of their sum. Net change was 0.078 (-0.066 to 0.243) of a matched spatial temperature benchmark. Six variants, including ten-survey endpoints and abundance weights, gave tracking point estimates from -0.027 to 0.127. All net-change intervals included zero. Independent historical scores thus support weak butterfly tracking. A small net index does not imply unchanged thermal composition. The distribution method measures cancellation without a reference species mean. It does not identify dispersal, habitat loss or pollution as causes. Finite sampling can create gross change, and conditional spatial intervals omit shared year shocks and score error. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and an external-data regeneration method are included.
